lines.text: Spunto Sandbox starts from one rule: the code in a box is not trusted.
It may be root, the all-powerful user, inside its box. Outside, that changes nothing. So the sandbox stacks walls.
The first wall is the virtual machine: its own kernel, its own disks, and KVM between it and the hardware.
The second is Firecracker: few devices, and a filter that lets it make only the system calls it needs.
The third is the jailer. Each Firecracker runs locked in a folder of its own, as a user of its own, with no special right.
Someone who broke out of the VM would land in an empty cell.
Fourth, limits: each box gets its share of processor, memory and network. One box cannot starve the others.
Last, the network. A box reaches the internet, but not the host, not the other boxes, not your local network, and not the cloud's metadata server, which hands out its keys.
And nothing reaches a box unless the host opens the way.
